patch.summary:
Choose AppDynamics only if your buying job matches “Cisco APM / observability — Infrastructure from ~$6/vCPU/mo; Premium (infra+apps) from $33” rather than incident.io's shape. Choose incident.io only if your buying job matches “Incident response — Basic Free; Team $15/user/mo annual ($19 monthly); Pro $25/user; on-ca” rather than AppDynamics's shape. Workflow advantage: AppDynamics leans observability-monitoring; incident.io leans incident-oncall. Trade-off: you gain focus on one product's motion at the cost of the other's adjacent coverage — no universal winner.

Major differences:
- Positioning: AppDynamics is Cisco APM / observability — Infrastructure from ~$6/vCPU/mo; Premium (infra+apps) from $33/vCPU/mo annual; Enterprise $50/vCPU; often Cisco ; incident.io is Incident response — Basic Free; Team $15/user/mo annual ($19 monthly); Pro $25/user; on-call add-on +$10–$20/user. Does not outrank PagerDut.
- Company-size focus: AppDynamics (mid-market, enterprise) vs incident.io (small-business, mid-market).
- Workflow coverage skew: AppDynamics-leaning observability-monitoring vs incident.io-leaning incident-oncall.
- Researched limits: AppDynamics — Does not outrank Datadog (8.6); incident.io — On-call paging is an add-on (+$10–$20/user), not included in the $15 Team floor.

Limitations — AppDynamics: Does not outrank Datadog (8.6); $6/vCPU Infrastructure is not the APM-relevant floor — Premium $33 is; incident.io: On-call paging is an add-on (+$10–$20/user), not included in the $15 Team floor; Does not outrank PagerDuty (8.0) as the incident-oncall award.

Poor-fit cases: AppDynamics is a poor fit when that limitation bites: Does not outrank Datadog (8.6) · incident.io is a poor fit when that limitation bites: On-call paging is an add-on (+$10–$20/user), not included in the $15 Team floor · Avoid AppDynamics if you actually need incident.io's motion (Incident response — Basic Free; Team $15/user/mo annual ($19 monthly); Pro $25/u)

Neither product has a completed hands-on product test on SoftwareGlimpse — this comparison is research/data-based only.
